title: Global residency intake scorer and caseflow
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Purpose: Create a lightweight, reproducible intake scorer and caseflow for enterprise region and data-residency requests. This ticket defines the scoring rubric, the intake form fields, triage flow, SLA expectations for responses, and a small automation to tag requests for self-serve vs sales-assisted paths. Goal is to reduce triage time to < 24h for standard asks and provide deterministic prioritization for roadmap planning.

Scope:
- New region requests (customer wants deployment in a new cloud region)
- Data residency / data sovereignty constraints (storage/processing residency)
- Failover / cross-region redundancy requests for enterprise customers
- Residency exceptions tied to contract terms (e.g., contractual residency SLAs)

Non-goals: detailed runbooks for infra provisioning, legal contract negotiation, network peering tasks (will reference those teams as owners).

Key outcomes & success metrics:
1) A scoring rubric that maps incoming requests to a numeric priority (0-100) and a recommended path: self-serve, product-scheduled, sales-assisted, or executive review.
2) A documented caseflow (triage -> tech review -> legal/security -> delivery) with ownership and expected TATs.
3) Automation rules in Zendesk/Linear labels for routing based on score and keywords.
4) Playbook usable by Solutions Eng, Sales, and PM on-rotation.

Scoring dimensions (first pass):
- Customer size & ARR at stake (weight: 25)
- Compliance/regulatory mandate (weight: 25)
- Latency/locality user impact (weight: 15)
- Revenue motion / contract (weight: 15)
- Technical effort (weight: 10; negative for complex infra changes)
- Strategic value (weight: 10)

Minimum data required on intake form:
- Customer name + account ID
- Contact(s) and SE owner
- Requested region(s) / residency requirement
- Desired go-live window and critical dates
- Business driver (compliance/regulatory, latency, sales motion)
- Estimated ARR or contract value influenced
- Any existing Dedicated/Private commitments

Acceptance criteria (see list field):
- Intake form fields validated and available in Zendesk/Support intake.
- Scoring formula encoded in a spreadsheet and exported to a simple Lambda that annotates tickets.
- Triage caseflow diagram and owner RACI in Confluence.
- Automation tags applied for scores >=80 (sales-assisted) and <=30 (self-serve) with documented overrides.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (2 wks): Draft rubric + sample cases + internal review with Legal/Infra/Sales.
- Phase 1 (3 wks): Implement intake form + spreadsheet + automation prototype; run shadow triage on last 90 days of requests to validate scoring distribution.
- Phase 2 (2 wks): Publish playbook, train Solutions Eng & Sales, enable automated routing.
- Phase 3 (ongoing): Quarterly calibration and metric review.

Open decisions to resolve in next sync:
- Exact numeric thresholds for “sales-assisted” vs “product-scheduled” (proposed: >=80 sales-assisted, 50-79 product-scheduled, <50 self-serve).
- Whether to treat Dedicated customers with active commits as automatic priority boost (+10).
- Data-residency requests that require legal contract changes must escalate to Enterprise Contracts by default.

Stakeholders / reviewers:
- Legal / Privacy: Priya Desai (review contracts/residency definitions)
- Security: Jonah Li (assess encryption/KMS requirements)
- Infrastructure: Mei Wong (assess infra effort, failover complexity)
- Solutions Eng: Marco Alvarez (input on sales-assisted workflows)
- Revenue Ops: Tanya Hill (input on ARR thresholds and customer tagging)

Traceability & links: use links field for artifacts, link to GitHub PR for automation once available.

Longer-term: incorporate a lightweight SLA engine in Console that surfaces residency availability per account (goal: Q4 2026).

decision_matrix_sample: Example A: Large EU enterprise (ARR > $1M), regulatory mandate (GDPR residency), low tech complexity => score 92 => sales-assisted + expedited legal path
Example B: Early-stage startup requesting AU region for latency (ARR < $250k), moderate tech work => score 47 => product-scheduled in next quarterly plan
Example C: Existing Dedicated customer with contract specifying region => automatic +10 boost; score moves from 65 to 75 => product-scheduled with priority handling
